bmt-2022-discrete-tiebreaker-01.title: Last digit is forced
bmt-2022-discrete-tiebreaker-01.body:
Choose the first digit ($9$ ways, $1$ to $9$) and the second digit ($10$ ways). Then the third digit must be $\equiv-a-b\pmod{10}$, which has exactly one solution in $0$ to $9$. Total $9\cdot10=90$.

**Answer: 90**

bmt-2022-discrete-tiebreaker-02.title: Digits must be $0$, $2$, $4$
bmt-2022-discrete-tiebreaker-02.body:
If $n$ has a digit $6$ or $8$, doubling it produces a carry of $1$ into the next place, so the next digit of $2n$ is (even)$+1$ = odd. (If the digit is the leading one, the carry creates a leading $1$, which is odd.) So $2n$ is not extra-even. Conversely, if all digits of $n$ lie in $\{0,2,4\}$, then $2n$ has digits in $\{0,4,8\}$ with no carries.

Count positive integers $\le2022$ with all digits in $\{0,2,4\}$: up to three digits, $3^3-1=26$ (excluding $0$). Four digits: they must start with $20$ followed by $\{0,2\}$ in the third place: third digit $0$ gives $3$ choices for the last digit ($2000,2002,2004$), third digit $2$ gives $2$ choices ($2020,2022$). So $26+5=31$.

**Answer: 31**

bmt-2022-discrete-tiebreaker-03.title: Wilson's theorem on blocks
bmt-2022-discrete-tiebreaker-03.body:
*Ones digit $7$:* the numbers $7+10i$, $i=0,\dots,99$ (i.e. $7,17,\dots,997$) are distinct mod $101$ because $\gcd(10,101)=1$; they include $707=7\cdot101\equiv0$ and miss exactly the nonzero residue of $1007\equiv-3$. Without $707$ they cover all nonzero residues except $-3$, so by Wilson's theorem their product is $\equiv(-1)(-3)^{-1}=3^{-1}$; the factor $707$ contributes $\frac{707}{101}=7$ after dividing by $101$. So $\frac{P_1}{101}\equiv7\cdot3^{-1}$.

*Hundreds digit $7$:* $700,\dots,799$ without $707$ cover all nonzero residues except $800\equiv-8$, so that product is $\equiv(-1)(-8)^{-1}=8^{-1}$.

*Overlap:* the numbers $707,717,\dots,797$ appear in both blocks but only once in $A$; $707$ was already handled, and $717\cdots797\equiv10\cdot20\cdots90\equiv72\pmod{101}$ must be divided out once.

Hence $\frac A{101}\equiv7\cdot3^{-1}\cdot8^{-1}\cdot72^{-1}=7\cdot1728^{-1}\equiv7\cdot11^{-1}\equiv7\cdot46\equiv19\pmod{101}$.

**Answer: 19**
